answer: An AI-agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a stake equal to the square of the controller existing identity count, so cost(n) grows as n squared. An attacker spinning up a gale of fakes must burn velvet-smooth capital that scales superlinearly, while the network beacon publicly verifies the cumulative stake before any attestation is accepted. Parallelization fails because the stake is bound to the actor, not per-identity flat fees.
